docs.title: Practical activity
docs.text:
Your Task:

  1. Create Local GeoJSON: In your project directory, create my_data.geojson containing the polygon FeatureCollection from Section 2.1.
  2. Setup Base Map: Create a minimal OpenLayers project with an OpenStreetMap TileLayer (XYZ source).
  3. Add Local Vector Layer: Add a VectorLayer consuming ./my_data.geojson using VectorSource and GeoJSON format.
  4. Style the Vector Features: Apply custom Fill and Stroke styles to your GeoJSON layer.
  5. Add a WMS Layer: Add an ImageLayer using ImageWMS connected to https://demo.geoserver.org/geoserver/wms with parameter LAYERS: 'ne:ne_10m_admin_0_countries'.
  6. Configure WMS Transparency: Set TRANSPARENT: true so the underlying OSM base map remains visible.
  7. Inspect the Network: Open your browser's Developer Tools (F12) and select the Network tab.
  8. Analyze Requests: Pan and zoom the map, then filter and observe:
  9. The initial GeoJSON request (loaded once via Fetch/XHR).
  10. The WMS image request (re-requested on pan/zoom with an updated bounding box).
  11. The XYZ tile requests (loading individual 256x256 image squares).
  12. Optional Bonus: Add a local GeoTIFF file using GeoTIFF source and WebGLTileLayer.

docs.title: Example Implementation (main.js):
docs.text:
import Map from 'ol/Map.js';
import View from 'ol/View.js';
import TileLayer from 'ol/layer/Tile.js';
import ImageLayer from 'ol/layer/Image.js';
import VectorLayer from 'ol/layer/Vector.js';
import OSM from 'ol/source/OSM.js';
import ImageWMS from 'ol/source/ImageWMS.js';
import VectorSource from 'ol/source/Vector.js';
import GeoJSON from 'ol/format/GeoJSON.js';
import { Style, Fill, Stroke } from 'ol/style.js';
import { fromLonLat } from 'ol/proj.js';
import 'ol/ol.css';

// 1. Base Layer: OpenStreetMap (XYZ Raster Tiles)
const osmLayer = new TileLayer({
  source: new OSM(),
  zIndex: 0
});

// 2. WMS Layer: Countries from GeoServer
const wmsLayer = new ImageLayer({
  source: new ImageWMS({
    url: 'https://demo.geoserver.org/geoserver/wms',
    params: {
      'LAYERS': 'ne:ne_10m_admin_0_countries',
      'TRANSPARENT': true,
      'FORMAT': 'image/png'
    },
    serverType: 'geoserver'
  }),
  opacity: 0.6,
  zIndex: 1
});

// 3. Vector Layer: Local GeoJSON
const vectorLayer = new VectorLayer({
  source: new VectorSource({
    features: new GeoJSON().readFeatures({
      type: 'FeatureCollection',
      features: [
        {
          type: 'Feature',
          properties: { name: 'Sample Region', category: 'Zone A' },
          geometry: {
            type: 'Polygon',
            coordinates: [
              [
                fromLonLat([73.85, 18.52]),
                fromLonLat([73.86, 18.52]),
                fromLonLat([73.86, 18.53]),
                fromLonLat([73.85, 18.53]),
                fromLonLat([73.85, 18.52])
              ]
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    })
  }),
  style: new Style({
    fill: new Fill({ color: 'rgba(255, 152, 0, 0.4)' }),
    stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#E65100', width: 2 })
  }),
  zIndex: 2
});

// 4. Initialize Map
const map = new Map({
  target: 'map',
  layers: [osmLayer, wmsLayer, vectorLayer],
  view: new View({
    center: fromLonLat([73.8567, 18.5204]),
    zoom: 12
  })
});

docs.title: Module 3 - GeoServer & PostGIS Enterprise Integration
docs.text:
Welcome to Module 3! In this module, we transition from standalone static files to the industry-standard enterprise Web GIS architecture: PostGIS as the spatial database engine, GeoServer as the publishing and middleware server, and OpenLayers as the high-performance client mapping library.

flowchart LR
    A[(PostGIS Database<br/>Spatial Storage & SQL)] -->|JDBC / GiST Index| B[GeoServer<br/>OGC Services: WMS / WFS / WMTS]
    B -->|WMS: Rendered Map Images| C[OpenLayers ImageLayer]
    B -->|WFS: Live GeoJSON Features| D[OpenLayers VectorLayer]
    C --> E[Browser Viewport]
    D --> E

docs.title: 1.1 The 3-Tier Enterprise Pipeline
docs.text:
In production spatial systems, data flows through three distinct operational tiers:

               ENTERPRISE 3-TIER ARCHITECTURE
Storage Tier:       PostgreSQL + PostGIS
                    (Raw Coordinates, GiST Spatial Indexes, Spatial SQL)
                                   ↓ (JDBC Connection Pool)
Middleware Tier:    GeoServer
                    (GeoTools Engine, SLD Cartography, OGC Services: WMS/WFS/WMTS)
                                   ↓ (HTTP / HTTPS Standards)
Client Tier:        OpenLayers
                    (HTML5 Canvas/WebGL Engine, Layer & Interaction Management)
                                   ↓
Presentation Tier:  Web Browser Viewport
  • Storage & Processing Tier (PostGIS): Stores millions of coordinate geometries, enforces topological rules, performs spatial joins, and filters records using R-Tree spatial indexes.
  • Middleware & Service Tier (GeoServer): Reads spatial tables, validates coordinate systems, calculates extents, styles data on the server via SLD, and exposes standardized OGC web service endpoints.
  • Client Tier (OpenLayers): Requests server-rendered map images (WMS) or raw vector geometries (WFS), handles smooth pan and zoom navigation, and provides interactive user tools.

docs.title: 1.2 Client-Side vs. Server-Side Spatial Processing
docs.text:
Processing Location Strengths Best Used For Server-Side (PostGIS) • Queries millions of records in milliseconds• Leverages GiST spatial indexes• Executes complex spatial joins and heavy geoprocessing • Spatial containment (ST_Within)• Proximity buffer analysis (ST_DWithin)• Large-scale spatial aggregation Client-Side (OpenLayers) • Zero network latency once loaded• Smooth 60 FPS animations and hover states• Instant user selection and measurement • Feature click popups & tooltips• Highlighting geometries under the mouse• Client-side dynamic styling and drawing

Key Architectural Rule: Always filter, clip, and aggregate as close to the database as possible. Never download 500,000 features over the network into OpenLayers when the user only needs to view 50.

docs.title: 2.1 PostgreSQL vs. PostGIS
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL: An open-source Object-Relational Database Management System (ORDBMS) offering ACID transactions, sophisticated concurrency, and enterprise reliability.
  • PostGIS: The spatial database extension for PostgreSQL that adheres to the OGC Simple Features for SQL (SFS) specification, adding:
  • Native spatial data types (geometry, geography, raster).
  • Over 1,000 spatial functions for measurement, relationships, and processing.
  • R-Tree spatial indexing via GiST (Generalized Search Tree).
  • Spatial reference system metadata (spatial_ref_sys).

docs.title: 2.2 PostGIS Spatial Data Types: geometry vs. geography
docs.text:
PostGIS Spatial Data Types
 ├── geometry   → Planar / Cartesian (Euclidean math, any projection: EPSG:3857, UTM, etc.)
 └── geography  → Geodetic / Spherical (Great Circle math, strictly WGS 84 EPSG:4326, meters)
Feature geometry geography Coordinate Space Flat Cartesian plane Curved sphere / ellipsoid Supported Projections Any CRS (EPSG:4326, EPSG:3857, UTM, State Plane) Strictly WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) Measurement Units Matches CRS units (meters for 3857/UTM; degrees for 4326) Always in meters automatically Performance Extremely fast; full spatial function catalog Slightly slower computation; focused function subset Typical Use City/regional maps, CAD/engineering, Web GIS Global flight paths, international maritime boundaries

docs.title: 2.3 Core OGC Geometry Types (WKT)
docs.text: PostGIS represents shapes using Well-Known Text (WKT): - POINT(73.8567 18.5204): Single coordinate point. - LINESTRING(73.85 18.52, 73.86 18.53, 73.87 18.55): Connected line segments. - POLYGON((73.85 18.52, 73.86 18.52, 73.86 18.53, 73.85 18.53, 73.85 18.52)): Closed polygon boundary. - Multi-Geometries: MULTIPOINT, MULTILINESTRING, MULTIPOLYGON, and heterogeneous GEOMETRYCOLLECTION.

docs.title: 2.4 SRID and Coordinate Reference Systems
docs.text:
An SRID (Spatial Reference System Identifier) identifies a coordinate reference system in the EPSG registry: - EPSG:4326 (WGS 84): Unprojected geographic coordinates in angular degrees (Longitude: -180 to +180, Latitude: -90 to +90). Used by GPS and GeoJSON. - EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator): Projected planar coordinates in meters. Used by Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, and OpenLayers default views. - Projected Grids (e.g., UTM Zone 43N - EPSG:32643): Conformal projections designed for meter-accurate distance and area measurements within a defined zone.

-- Convert WGS 84 degrees into Web Mercator planar meters:
SELECT id, ST_Transform(geom, 3857) AS geom_3857
FROM buildings;

-- Set SRID metadata if missing (does NOT change coordinate values):
SELECT ST_SetSRID(ST_Point(73.8567, 18.5204), 4326);

docs.title: 2.5 Essential PostGIS Spatial Functions
docs.text: Function Description Return Type ST_Area(geom) Computes the area of a polygon in CRS units double precision ST_Length(geom) Computes line length in CRS units double precision ST_Centroid(geom) Computes the geometric center point geometry (Point) ST_Buffer(geom, radius) Creates a boundary buffer of radius units geometry (Polygon) ST_Intersects(geomA, geomB) Returns true if geometries share any space boolean ST_Within(geomA, geomB) Returns true if A is completely inside B boolean ST_Contains(geomA, geomB) Returns true if A completely encloses B boolean ST_DWithin(geomA, geomB, dist) Returns true if geometries are within dist units (Index-accelerated) boolean ST_Distance(geomA, geomB) Returns minimum 2D distance between geometries double precision

docs.title: 2.6 Spatial Indexing with GiST (R-Trees)
docs.text:
Spatial shapes have no natural 1D order. Finding which polygons intersect without an index requires comparing every single vertex against all records. PostGIS resolves this using GiST (Generalized Search Tree) indexes based on R-Trees, indexing the 2D Bounding Box (Envelope) of each geometry.

CREATE INDEX buildings_geom_idx ON buildings USING GIST (geom);

docs.title: Two-Stage Query Processing
docs.text: When executing a spatial query like ST_Intersects(buildings.geom, parcel.geom): 1. Stage 1 (Index Filter): PostGIS uses the GiST index to compare bounding boxes (&&). This instantly eliminates 99.9% of geometries that do not touch. 2. Stage 2 (Exact Test): PostGIS runs exact point-in-polygon vertex math only on the surviving candidate records.

docs.title: 3.1 What is GeoServer?
docs.text: GeoServer is an open-source Java application that shares and edits geospatial data according to OGC standards. Built on top of the GeoTools spatial engine, GeoServer connects to spatial databases, renders map graphics, and publishes services.

docs.title: 3.2 GeoServer Data Hierarchy
docs.text:
GeoServer organizes spatial data into a four-level administrative structure:

Workspace (Logical department container & XML namespace)
   └── Store (Physical connection to PostGIS database or directory)
        └── Layer / FeatureType (Individual spatial table or file)
             └── Style (SLD cartographic symbology rules)
  • Workspace: Groups related stores and layers together (e.g., training). Layer qualified names take the form workspace:layer_name (e.g., training:roads, training:buildings).
  • Store: Connection configuration to the data source (PostGIS database, Directory of Shapefiles, GeoPackage, or GeoTIFF).
  • Layer / Resource: The published dataset with verified CRS, bounding boxes, and assigned style.
  • Layer Group: A combined endpoint that packages multiple layers together in a single request.

docs.title: 3.3 Connecting PostGIS to GeoServer
docs.text:
1. In PostgreSQL, ensure the extension is active: 
    CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;
  2. In GeoServer Admin: Stores → Add new Store → PostGIS (Vector Data DataStore).
  3. Enter connection parameters: Host (localhost), Port (5432), Database (gis_training), Schema (public), Username, and Password.
  4. Save the store.

docs.title: 3.4 Publishing a Layer (The 8-Step Workflow)
docs.text:
1. Create Workspace → 2. Add Store → 3. Select Table → 4. Publish Layer
        ↓
5. Verify CRS → 6. Calculate Bounding Boxes → 7. Configure Style → 8. Layer Preview
  • Verify CRS: Ensure Native CRS is detected (e.g., EPSG:4326). If unknown, set Declared CRS and choose Force Declared.
  • Compute Bounding Boxes: Click Compute from data (Native Bounding Box) and Compute from native bounds (Lat/Lon Bounding Box). If bounding boxes are missing or zero, OpenLayers will not display the layer.
  • Assign Style: Select a default SLD style under the Publishing tab.
  • Preview: Verify the layer in GeoServer's Layer Preview list.

docs.title: 3.5 GeoServer SQL Views
docs.text:
GeoServer allows publishing raw PostGIS SQL queries as independent map layers. - Static SQL View: Pre-filters records or runs spatial operations on the database before GeoServer draws them (e.g. querying Natural Earth populated_places): 

SELECT id, name, adm0name, pop_max, ST_Buffer(geom, 0.5) AS geom
FROM populated_places
WHERE pop_max >= 1000000;
- Parameterized SQL View: Accepts dynamic arguments at runtime using %param% syntax: 
SELECT id, name, adm0name, pop_max, geom
FROM populated_places
WHERE pop_max >= %min_population%
In OpenLayers, pass values via the WMS VIEWPARAMS property: 
wmsSource.updateParams({ 'VIEWPARAMS': 'min_population:5000000' });

docs.title: 4. Service Metadata & GetCapabilities
docs.text:
Before writing client-side code, inspect GeoServer's GetCapabilities XML document:

  • WMS: http://localhost:8080/geoserver/wms?service=WMS&version=1.3.0&request=GetCapabilities
  • WFS: http://localhost:8080/geoserver/wfs?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetCapabilities

docs.title: Key XML Elements to Inspect:
docs.text:
• <Layer><Name>training:roads</Name></Layer>: The exact identifier needed for LAYERS in OpenLayers.
  • <CRS>: Supported projections (e.g., EPSG:3857, EPSG:4326).
  • <Format>: Supported image formats (image/png, image/jpeg) or vector formats (application/json).
  • <EX_GeographicBoundingBox>: Min/Max Longitude and Latitude limits.

docs.title: 5. Consuming GeoServer WMS in OpenLayers
docs.text: WMS (Web Map Service) renders map images on the server and returns raster pictures to OpenLayers.

docs.title: 5.1 ImageWMS vs. TileWMS
docs.text:
• ImageWMS (Single Image): Requests a single image covering the entire map canvas for the current extent. Prevents text labels from being chopped across tile borders.
  • TileWMS (Tiled Images): Requests a grid of 256×256 pixel tiles. Best for base maps and cached layers via GeoWebCache.

docs.title: 5.2 Key WMS Request Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Purpose Example LAYERS Qualified layer name on GeoServer 'training:roads' STYLES Named SLD style on server (blank for default) '' FORMAT Output MIME format 'image/png' TRANSPARENT Allows underlying base maps to show through true VERSION OGC WMS version '1.3.0'

docs.title: 5.3 OpenLayers WMS Implementation
docs.text:
import ImageLayer from 'ol/layer/Image.js';
import ImageWMS from 'ol/source/ImageWMS.js';

const wmsSource = new ImageWMS({
  url: 'http://localhost:8080/geoserver/wms',
  params: {
    'LAYERS': 'training:roads',
    'TRANSPARENT': true,
    'FORMAT': 'image/png'
  },
  serverType: 'geoserver' // Enables vendor optimizations
});

const wmsLayer = new ImageLayer({
  source: wmsSource,
  opacity: 0.85
});

map.addLayer(wmsLayer);

docs.title: 5.4 Dynamic WMS Filtering with CQL
docs.text:
GeoServer supports CQL (Common Query Language), allowing OpenLayers to filter server-side data dynamically:

// Apply filter: show only highways with 4 or more lanes
wmsSource.updateParams({
  'CQL_FILTER': "type = 'highway' AND lanes >= 4"
});

// Clear filter: show all features
wmsSource.updateParams({
  'CQL_FILTER': null
});

docs.title: 5.5 WMS Feature Inspection (GetFeatureInfo)
docs.text:
Because WMS layers are flat raster images, OpenLayers asks GeoServer what feature exists at a clicked coordinate via getFeatureInfoUrl:

map.on('singleclick', (evt) => {
  const viewResolution = map.getView().getResolution();
  const url = wmsSource.getFeatureInfoUrl(
    evt.coordinate,
    viewResolution,
    'EPSG:3857',
    { 'INFO_FORMAT': 'application/json' }
  );

  if (url) {
    fetch(url)
      .then((res) => res.json())
      .then((data) => {
        if (data.features.length > 0) {
          const props = data.features[0].properties;
          alert(`Selected: ${props.name || 'Unnamed'}`);
        }
      });
  }
});

docs.title: 6. Consuming GeoServer WFS in OpenLayers
docs.text:
WFS (Web Feature Service) streams raw vector geometries and attributes (typically GeoJSON) into the browser.

GeoServer WFS → GeoJSON → ol/source/Vector → ol/layer/Vector → Browser Canvas

docs.title: 6.1 Loading WFS with Viewport Bounding Box Strategy
docs.text:
Downloading thousands of features at once can freeze the browser. Use ol/loadingstrategy.bbox so OpenLayers only requests features within the current screen extent:

import VectorSource from 'ol/source/Vector.js';
import VectorLayer from 'ol/layer/Vector.js';
import GeoJSON from 'ol/format/GeoJSON.js';
import { bbox as bboxStrategy } from 'ol/loadingstrategy.js';
import { Style, Stroke, Fill } from 'ol/style.js';

const wfsSource = new VectorSource({
  format: new GeoJSON(),
  strategy: bboxStrategy,
  loader: function (extent, resolution, projection) {
    const proj = projection.getCode();
    const url = `http://localhost:8080/geoserver/wfs?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetFeature&typeNames=training:buildings&outputFormat=application/json&srsname=${proj}&bbox=${extent.join(',')},${proj}`;

    fetch(url)
      .then((res) => res.json())
      .then((data) => {
        wfsSource.addFeatures(new GeoJSON().readFeatures(data));
      });
  }
});

const wfsLayer = new VectorLayer({
  source: wfsSource,
  style: new Style({
    stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#1565C0', width: 2 }),
    fill: new Fill({ color: 'rgba(33, 150, 243, 0.3)' })
  })
});

map.addLayer(wfsLayer);

docs.title: 7. WMS vs. WFS Decision Matrix
docs.text: Requirement / Capability WMS (Web Map Service) WFS (Web Feature Service) Output Type Image picture (PNG, JPEG) Raw vector geometry (GeoJSON) Browser Workload Very Low Higher (processes coordinates & DOM paths) Large Datasets (> 50,000 features) Best Choice Unsuitable (high network & memory usage) Interactive Feature Popups Via GetFeatureInfo server call Instant client-side inspection Client-Side Hover / Dynamic Styling ❌ No ✅ Yes Feature Geometry Editing ❌ No ✅ Yes (via WFS-T) Network Payload Size Constant (size of one screen image) Proportional to feature count

docs.title: 8.1 Performance Best Practices
docs.text:
• Index All Geometry Columns: Always build GiST indexes on PostGIS tables (CREATE INDEX ... USING GIST(geom)).
  • Filter Early: Filter at the database tier using SQL Views or PostGIS WHERE clauses rather than sending raw data to the client.
  • Use BBOX Loading: Always use loadingstrategy.bbox with WFS vector sources.
  • Run Maintenance: Periodically run VACUUM ANALYZE table_name; in PostgreSQL so the query planner generates optimal spatial plans.

docs.title: 8.2 Diagnostic Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Issue[Layer Fails to Render] --> Step1[Check GeoServer Layer Preview]
    Step1 -->|Fails in GeoServer| Fix1[Check Store Connection, Native CRS, and Bounding Boxes]
    Step1 -->|Works in GeoServer| Step2[Inspect Browser Network Tab F12]
    Step2 -->|HTTP 404| Fix2[Verify Service URL & workspace:layer name spelling]
    Step2 -->|HTTP 400| Fix3[Check XML ServiceExceptionReport: BBOX or CRS syntax error]
    Step2 -->|CORS Error| Fix4[Uncomment CORS filter in GeoServer web.xml and restart Tomcat]
    Step2 -->|HTTP 200 Blank Image| Fix5[Check Map View Center/Extent & CQL_FILTER conditions]

docs.title: Reference Resources
docs.text:
• PostGIS Official Documentation: https://postgis.net/docs/
  • GeoServer User Manual: https://docs.geoserver.org/
  • OpenLayers ImageWMS API: https://openlayers.org/en/latest/apidoc/module-ol_source_ImageWMS-ImageWMS.html
  • OpenLayers VectorSource API: https://openlayers.org/en/latest/apidoc/module-ol_source_Vector-VectorSource.html

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Build an enterprise pipeline connecting PostGIS, GeoServer, and OpenLayers using the Natural Earth Populated Places dataset: 1. Verify spatial data in PostGIS with spatial SQL (SELECT name, pop_max FROM populated_places LIMIT 10;). 2. Publish the populated_places layer in GeoServer (workspace: training, calculate bounding boxes, point style). 3. Display the layer in OpenLayers using ImageWMS over OpenStreetMap. 4. Add dynamic CQL filtering via a UI button to filter Megacities (pop_max >= 5000000). 5. Implement GetFeatureInfo on map click to display city attributes (Name, Country, Population) in an alert or popup.

docs.title: Complete Example Implementation (main.js):
docs.text:
import Map from 'ol/Map.js';
import View from 'ol/View.js';
import TileLayer from 'ol/layer/Tile.js';
import ImageLayer from 'ol/layer/Image.js';
import OSM from 'ol/source/OSM.js';
import ImageWMS from 'ol/source/ImageWMS.js';
import { fromLonLat } from 'ol/proj.js';
import 'ol/ol.css';

// 1. Base Layer: OpenStreetMap
const osmBase = new TileLayer({
  source: new OSM(),
  zIndex: 0
});

// 2. Enterprise GeoServer WMS Layer: Natural Earth Populated Places
const postgisWmsSource = new ImageWMS({
  url: 'http://localhost:8080/geoserver/wms',
  params: {
    'LAYERS': 'training:populated_places',
    'TRANSPARENT': true,
    'FORMAT': 'image/png'
  },
  serverType: 'geoserver'
});

const placesLayer = new ImageLayer({
  source: postgisWmsSource,
  opacity: 0.9,
  zIndex: 1
});

// 3. Initialize OpenLayers Map (Centered on global or regional view)
const map = new Map({
  target: 'map',
  layers: [osmBase, placesLayer],
  view: new View({
    center: fromLonLat([0, 20]),
    zoom: 3
  })
});

// 4. Dynamic CQL Filter: Show only Megacities (pop_max >= 5,000,000)
const filterButton = document.getElementById('filter-megacities');
if (filterButton) {
  let isFiltered = false;
  filterButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
    isFiltered = !isFiltered;
    postgisWmsSource.updateParams({
      'CQL_FILTER': isFiltered ? 'pop_max >= 5000000' : null
    });
    filterButton.textContent = isFiltered ? 'Show All Cities' : 'Show Megacities (5M+)';
  });
}

// 5. Query Feature Attributes on Click (GetFeatureInfo)
map.on('singleclick', (event) => {
  const viewResolution = map.getView().getResolution();
  const infoUrl = postgisWmsSource.getFeatureInfoUrl(
    event.coordinate,
    viewResolution,
    'EPSG:3857',
    { 'INFO_FORMAT': 'application/json' }
  );

  if (infoUrl) {
    fetch(infoUrl)
      .then((res) => res.json())
      .then((data) => {
        if (data.features && data.features.length > 0) {
          const props = data.features[0].properties;
          const cityName = props.name || props.NAME || 'City';
          const country = props.adm0name || props.ADM0NAME || 'N/A';
          const population = props.pop_max ? Number(props.pop_max).toLocaleString() : 'N/A';
          alert(`City: ${cityName}\nCountry: ${country}\nPopulation: ${population}`);
        }
      })
      .catch((err) => console.error('GetFeatureInfo Error:', err));
  }
});

docs.title: Module 4 - Vector Styling & Feature Interaction
docs.text:
Welcome to Module 4! In this module, we transition from merely loading raw vector coordinates to crafting expressive, responsive, and interactive Web GIS interfaces. We will follow the complete production engineering workflow:

Feature Data & Geometry
          ↓
Dynamic Style Function (with Caching & Decluttering)
          ↓
Symbology, Halo Labels & Custom Icons
          ↓
Canvas Pointer Detection (Hover Highlight & Cursor State)
          ↓
Selection Interaction & Coordinate-Anchored Popups

docs.title: 1.1 Why Vector Styling is Different from WMS Styling
docs.text:
In Module 3, we explored server-side WMS styling via GeoServer SLD, where the server renders features into static pixels before sending them across the network. Vector styling in OpenLayers is fundamentally different:

Feature Server-Side WMS Styling (GeoServer / SLD) Client-Side Vector Styling (OpenLayers) Rendering Engine Server CPU / GPU (GeoServer) Browser HTML5 Canvas / WebGL Output Type Pre-rendered raster image (PNG, JPEG) Live DOM / Canvas vector paths Interactivity Requires server roundtrips (GetFeatureInfo) Instant client-side inspection, selection & hover Styling Flexibility Static XML rules on the server Full JavaScript logic (conditional, dynamic, animated) Styling Speed Re-requests images on style changes Updates instantly in browser memory Data Payload Map image pixels Raw coordinates and attributes (GeoJSON/WFS)

docs.title: 1.2 Client-Side Styling in OpenLayers
docs.text:
In OpenLayers, vector layers use the setStyle() method to apply visual symbology. Styling can be assigned at two distinct scopes:

  • VectorLayer: vectorLayer.setStyle(...) sets the default appearance for all features on the layer.
  • Individual Feature: feature.setStyle(...) overrides the layer style for a specific feature instance (ideal for selection flags, hover highlights, or custom status indicators).

docs.title: 1.3 Static vs. Dynamic Styling
docs.text:
• Static Styling: A fixed Style object applied uniformly to every feature across all zoom levels.
  • Dynamic Styling: A JavaScript Style Function that inspects each feature's attributes (feature.get('type')) or the map's current zoom resolution to return tailored styles dynamically.

docs.title: 1.4 Geometry Targets
docs.text:
Styles apply across the three core vector geometry categories:

  • Point / MultiPoint: Styled with circular vector symbols (Circle) or external bitmap/SVG graphics (Icon).
  • LineString / MultiLineString: Styled with strokes (Stroke).
  • Polygon / MultiPolygon: Styled with interior fills (Fill) and outer boundary strokes (Stroke).

docs.title: 2. OpenLayers Style Components
docs.text:
OpenLayers builds symbology using specialized building blocks imported from ol/style.js:

Point Feature
 ├── image: Circle / Icon
 └── text:  Text (Label)

LineString Feature
 ├── stroke: Stroke (Color, Width, Dash)
 └── text:   Text (Label)

Polygon Feature
 ├── fill:   Fill (Color, Opacity)
 ├── stroke: Stroke (Boundary)
 └── text:   Text (Centroid Label)

docs.title: 2.1 Core Style Classes
docs.text:
• Style: The root container that groups together fill, stroke, image, and text symbolizers.
  • Fill: Defines interior colors and transparencies for polygons, circles, and text backgrounds. Supports HEX, RGB, RGBA, and HSL strings.
  • Stroke: Defines boundary lines, road paths, and outlines with width, color, and dash patterns.
  • Circle (CircleStyle): Vector circular marker designed specifically for Point geometries.
  • Icon: External raster (PNG/JPEG) or vector (SVG) image symbol for Point geometries.
  • Text: Renders dynamic typographic labels anchored to feature geometries.

docs.title: 2.2 Core Style Properties Reference
docs.text: Component Property Description Example Fill Fill color HEX, RGB, RGBA, or HSL color string color: 'rgba(33, 150, 243, 0.5)' Stroke Stroke color Outline line color color: '#1565C0' Stroke width Line thickness in pixels width: 2.5 Line dash Dash-gap array pattern lineDash: [6, 6] (6px dash, 6px space) Circle Point radius Radius of circle marker in pixels radius: 8 Icon Icon image URL or path to image file src: '/icons/hospital.svg' Scale Scaling factor scale: 0.8 Anchor Alignment point coordinates anchor: [0.5, 1] (Bottom-center pin) Rotation Rotation angle in radians rotation: Math.PI / 4 Text Text font Font style, size, and family font: 'bold 13px Inter, sans-serif' Text color Color of the text characters fill: new Fill({ color: '#212121' }) Text offset Pixel displacement (X, Y) offsetY: -15 (Places text above marker)

docs.title: 3. Static Styling
docs.text: When all features in a layer share identical cartography, apply a single reusable Style object to the VectorLayer.

docs.title: 3.1 Applying Styles to Points, Lines, and Polygons
docs.text:
import VectorLayer from 'ol/layer/Vector.js';
import VectorSource from 'ol/source/Vector.js';
import { Style, Fill, Stroke, Circle as CircleStyle } from 'ol/style.js';

// 1. Polygon Style (Fills and Outlines)
const parcelStyle = new Style({
  fill: new Fill({
    color: 'rgba(76, 175, 80, 0.3)'
  }),
  stroke: new Stroke({
    color: '#2E7D32',
    width: 2
  })
});

// 2. LineString Style (Roads / Rivers)
const roadStyle = new Style({
  stroke: new Stroke({
    color: '#FF9800',
    width: 3,
    lineDash: [4, 4]
  })
});

// 3. Point Style (Circular Marker)
const pointStyle = new Style({
  image: new CircleStyle({
    radius: 7,
    fill: new Fill({ color: '#E91E63' }),
    stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 2 })
  })
});

// Apply style to VectorLayer
const vectorLayer = new VectorLayer({
  source: new VectorSource({ /* ... */ }),
  style: parcelStyle
});

docs.title: 3.2 The Importance of Reusable Style Objects
docs.text:
Always define style objects outside render loops:

vectorLayer.setStyle(myStyle);

The Mechanics of Reusable Styles: OpenLayers executes the styling pipeline every time a frame is rendered (during pan, zoom, or animations at 60 FPS). Reusing pre-instantiated style objects prevents allocating thousands of temporary JavaScript objects, avoiding browser garbage-collection pauses and stuttering animations.

docs.title: 4. Attribute-Based Dynamic Styling
docs.text: Real-world applications require thematic styling where feature appearance reflects underlying attributes.

docs.title: 4.1 Reading Feature Attributes
docs.text:
Feature attributes are accessed using .get(): 

const category = feature.get('type');
const population = feature.get('population');

docs.title: 4.2 Dynamic Style Function
docs.text:
Pass a function to vectorLayer.setStyle(). OpenLayers evaluates the function for each feature:

const styleFunction = (feature) => {
  const type = feature.get('type');

  if (type === 'hospital') {
    return hospitalStyle;
  }

  if (type === 'school') {
    return schoolStyle;
  }

  return defaultStyle;
};

vectorLayer.setStyle(styleFunction);

docs.title: 4.3 Categorized Thematic Styling
docs.text:
Pre-define reusable styles in a lookup table for maximum efficiency:

const facilityStyles = {
  hospital: new Style({
    image: new CircleStyle({
      radius: 8,
      fill: new Fill({ color: '#D32F2F' }), // Red
      stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 2 })
    })
  }),
  school: new Style({
    image: new CircleStyle({
      radius: 8,
      fill: new Fill({ color: '#1976D2' }), // Blue
      stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 2 })
    })
  }),
  default: new Style({
    image: new CircleStyle({
      radius: 6,
      fill: new Fill({ color: '#757575' }), // Gray
      stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 1.5 })
    })
  })
};

vectorLayer.setStyle((feature) => {
  const category = feature.get('type');
  return facilityStyles[category] || facilityStyles.default;
});

docs.title: 4.4 Basic Graduated Styling (Numeric Ranges)
docs.text:
Adjust visual properties (color, size) based on numeric attributes:

function earthquakeStyle(feature) {
  const mag = feature.get('magnitude');

  let color = '#4CAF50'; // Low < 4.0
  let radius = 5;

  if (mag >= 6.0) {
    color = '#D32F2F'; // Severe >= 6.0
    radius = 12;
  } else if (mag >= 4.0) {
    color = '#FB8C00'; // Moderate 4.0 - 5.9
    radius = 8;
  }

  return new Style({
    image: new CircleStyle({
      radius: radius,
      fill: new Fill({ color: color }),
      stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 1.5 })
    })
  });
}

docs.title: 5. Text Labels
docs.text:
Labels display contextual information directly on the map.

new Text({
  text: feature.get('name'),
  font: '14px sans-serif',
  offsetY: -15
});

docs.title: 5.1 Label Configuration
docs.text:
• text: The string to display, typically retrieved from a feature attribute (feature.get('name')).
  • font: Standard CSS font string (e.g., 'bold 12px Inter, sans-serif').
  • fill: Font character color (new Fill({ color: '#212121' })).
  • stroke: Outer halo around letters (new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 3 })). Critical for legibility over satellite imagery and street maps.
  • backgroundFill / backgroundStroke: Optional background pill box behind the text.
  • offsetY / offsetX: Pixel displacement relative to the feature geometry center.

docs.title: 5.2 Scale & Visibility Control
docs.text:
Displaying thousands of labels when zoomed out causes visual clutter and slows rendering. Use the resolution argument in your style function to display labels only when zoomed in close:

vectorLayer.setStyle((feature, resolution) => {
  // Only show text labels when resolution is less than 30 meters/pixel (zoomed in)
  const showLabel = resolution < 30;

  return new Style({
    image: pointMarker,
    text: showLabel ? new Text({
      text: feature.get('name') || '',
      font: 'bold 12px sans-serif',
      fill: new Fill({ color: '#111111' }),
      stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 3 }),
      offsetY: -15
    }) : undefined
  });
});

docs.title: 5.3 Automated Label Decluttering
docs.text:
OpenLayers features built-in collision detection to automatically hide overlapping labels and icons. Enable decluttering directly on the VectorLayer:

const declutteredLayer = new VectorLayer({
  source: vectorSource,
  style: featureStyleFunction,
  declutter: true // Automatically hides colliding text labels and icons
});

docs.title: 6. Icons & Custom Symbols
docs.text:
Vector points can be styled with custom bitmap (PNG) or vector (SVG) images using ol/style/Icon.

Common Web GIS Use Cases:
 Hospital → hospital icon
 School   → school icon
 Airport  → airport icon

docs.title: 6.1 Creating an Icon Style
docs.text:
import { Style, Icon } from 'ol/style.js';

const hospitalIconStyle = new Style({
  image: new Icon({
    src: '/assets/icons/hospital.svg',
    anchor: [0.5, 1],          // Bottom-center pin tip aligns with coordinate
    anchorXUnits: 'fraction',
    anchorYUnits: 'fraction',
    scale: 0.8,                // Resizes icon
    rotation: 0                // Rotation in radians
  })
});

docs.title: 6.2 Anchor Positioning
docs.text:
The anchor property dictates which point of the icon image aligns with the feature's geographic coordinate:

  • [0.5, 0.5] (Center): Default. Best for circular badges, POI symbols, and airport markers.
  • [0.5, 1.0] (Bottom-Center): Standard for map pin markers so the needle tip points to the location.
       ┌──────────┐
       │  HOSPITAL│
       └────┬─────┘
            ▼  ← Anchor [0.5, 1.0] aligns with geographic coordinate

docs.title: 7. Feature Selection
docs.text:
OpenLayers provides the Select interaction (ol/interaction/Select) to capture user clicks, manage selection state, and highlight active features.

import Select from 'ol/interaction/Select.js';
import { click } from 'ol/events/condition.js';
import { Style, Fill, Stroke } from 'ol/style.js';

// 1. Configure the selection interaction
const select = new Select({
  condition: click, // Trigger on mouse click
  style: new Style({
    fill: new Fill({ color: 'rgba(255, 235, 59, 0.5)' }),
    stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#F57F17', width: 3.5 })
  })
});

map.addInteraction(select);

// 2. Listen to the select event
select.on('select', (event) => {
  const feature = event.selected[0];

  if (feature) {
    console.log('Selected feature properties:', feature.getProperties());
  }
});

docs.title: 7.1 Selection Features
docs.text:
• Selection Condition: condition: click triggers on single clicks; pointerMove triggers on hover.
  • Deselection: Clicking anywhere on the empty map canvas automatically deselects features.
  • Selected Array: event.selected contains features just selected; event.deselected contains features whose selection was cleared.

docs.title: 8. Hover Interaction
docs.text:
Hover effects provide instant visual feedback as the user navigates across the map canvas.

Mouse moves (pointermove)
     ↓
Feature detected?
     ↓
    Yes
     ↓
Apply highlight style & change cursor to pointer

docs.title: 8.1 Changing the Mouse Cursor
docs.text:
Inform the user when an element is interactive by updating CSS cursor styling on pointermove:

map.on('pointermove', (evt) => {
  if (evt.dragging) return;

  const hit = map.hasFeatureAtPixel(evt.pixel);
  map.getTargetElement().style.cursor = hit ? 'pointer' : '';
});

docs.title: 8.2 Highlighting Features on Hover
docs.text:
let currentHoveredFeature = null;

const hoverHighlightStyle = new Style({
  stroke: new Stroke({
    color: '#00E5FF',
    width: 4
  })
});

map.on('pointermove', (evt) => {
  if (evt.dragging) return;

  // 1. Reset previous hovered feature
  if (currentHoveredFeature) {
    currentHoveredFeature.setStyle(null); // Reverts back to layer style
    currentHoveredFeature = null;
  }

  // 2. Highlight new feature under cursor
  map.forEachFeatureAtPixel(evt.pixel, (feature, layer) => {
    if (layer === vectorLayer) {
      currentHoveredFeature = feature;
      feature.setStyle(hoverHighlightStyle); // Apply feature-level highlight
      return true; // Stop iterating
    }
  });
});

docs.title: 9. Feature Information / Popup
docs.text:
Popups display detailed attributes in an HTML card anchored to the feature's coordinate using ol/Overlay.

User clicks feature
        ↓
Feature selected
        ↓
Read properties (feature.getProperties())
        ↓
Create popup content
        ↓
Display information at coordinate

docs.title: 9.1 Popup Setup (main.js)
docs.text:
import Overlay from 'ol/Overlay.js';

// 1. HTML DOM elements
const container = document.getElementById('popup');
const content = document.getElementById('popup-content');
const closer = document.getElementById('popup-closer');

// 2. Instantiate Overlay
const popupOverlay = new Overlay({
  element: container,
  autoPan: { animation: { duration: 250 } }
});
map.addOverlay(popupOverlay);

// 3. Close button
closer.onclick = () => {
  popupOverlay.setPosition(undefined);
  closer.blur();
  return false;
};

// 4. Click interaction to display popup
map.on('singleclick', (evt) => {
  const feature = map.forEachFeatureAtPixel(evt.pixel, (feat) => feat);

  if (feature) {
    const props = feature.getProperties();
    content.innerHTML = `
      <h4 style="margin: 0 0 6px 0;">${props.name || 'Feature'}</h4>
      <p style="margin: 0; font-size: 13px; color: #555;"><strong>Type:</strong> ${props.type || 'N/A'}</p>
    `;
    popupOverlay.setPosition(evt.coordinate);
  } else {
    popupOverlay.setPosition(undefined);
  }
});

docs.title: 10. Layer-Level vs. Feature-Level Styling
docs.text:
Understanding how style inheritance operates ensures optimal performance and modular code:

// Layer-level styling
vectorLayer.setStyle(...)

versus:

// Feature-level styling
feature.setStyle(...)
Scope Invocation Characteristics Primary Use Cases Layer-Level vectorLayer.setStyle(...) • Applied globally across all features• Highest rendering efficiency• Evaluated dynamically with style functions Default layer symbology, thematic classification, zoom-dependent scales Feature-Level feature.setStyle(...) • Overrides the layer style for a specific feature instance• Reverts when set to null: feature.setStyle(null) Temporary hover highlights, active selection flags, custom pin icons

docs.title: 11. Styling Performance
docs.text:
When rendering vector layers in production, keep these performance principles in mind:

  • Reuse Style Objects: Maintain a cached object dictionary (styles[category]) rather than constructing new Style() instances inside style functions.
  • Avoid Creating Complex Styles Unnecessarily: Every extra stroke, text shadow, and nested fill increases canvas draw call time.
  • Don't Use Huge Numbers of Unique Icons: Loading 200 distinct icon URLs triggers 200 separate asynchronous image downloads. Prefer SVG icons or standardized icon sheets.
  • Avoid Excessive Labels: Restrict label rendering to close zoom levels using the resolution argument or enable declutter: true.
  • Be Careful with Thousands of Client-Side Features: If your dataset exceeds 5,000 features, pure GeoJSON/WFS rendering can degrade browser frame rates.
  • Use Server-Side / Vector Tiles for Very Large Datasets: As covered in Module 2, switch to Vector Tiles (MVT) or server-side WMS for datasets with tens of thousands of geometries.

docs.title: Reference resources
docs.text:
• OpenLayers Style API: https://openlayers.org/en/latest/apidoc/module-ol_style_Style-Style.html
  • OpenLayers Select Interaction: https://openlayers.org/en/latest/apidoc/module-ol_interaction_Select-Select.html
  • OpenLayers Overlay API: https://openlayers.org/en/latest/apidoc/module-ol_Overlay-Overlay.html
  • OpenLayers Vector Labels Example: https://openlayers.org/en/latest/examples/vector-labels.html

docs.title: Step 1 — Dynamic Styling
docs.text:
1. Take the vector layer (GeoJSON or WFS) and apply a dynamic style function based on the type attribute: 
    vectorLayer.setStyle((feature) => {
  const type = feature.get('type');

  return type === 'hospital'
    ? hospitalStyle
    : defaultStyle;
});

docs.title: Step 2 — Labels
docs.text:
1. Extend the style function to display the feature's name attribute using new Text(): 
    new Text({
  text: feature.get('name'),
  font: 'bold 12px sans-serif',
  offsetY: -15
});

docs.title: Step 3 — Select Interaction
docs.text:
1. Add an OpenLayers Select interaction configured to trigger on click: 
    const select = new Select({
  condition: click
});
map.addInteraction(select);

select.on('select', (event) => {
  const feature = event.selected[0];

  if (feature) {
    console.log('Selected Properties:', feature.getProperties());
  }
});

docs.title: Step 4 — Bonus (Hover Effect)
docs.text: 1. Add a hover interaction that changes the mouse cursor to 'pointer' and applies a stroke highlight when the mouse moves over a feature.

docs.title: Example Implementation (main.js):
docs.text:
import Map from 'ol/Map.js';
import View from 'ol/View.js';
import TileLayer from 'ol/layer/Tile.js';
import VectorLayer from 'ol/layer/Vector.js';
import OSM from 'ol/source/OSM.js';
import VectorSource from 'ol/source/Vector.js';
import GeoJSON from 'ol/format/GeoJSON.js';
import Overlay from 'ol/Overlay.js';
import Select from 'ol/interaction/Select.js';
import { click } from 'ol/events/condition.js';
import { Style, Circle as CircleStyle, Fill, Stroke, Text } from 'ol/style.js';
import { fromLonLat } from 'ol/proj.js';
import 'ol/ol.css';

// 1. Base Map Layer
const baseLayer = new TileLayer({
  source: new OSM()
});

// 2. Pre-defined Reusable Styles (Natural Earth Populated Places)
const capitalStyle = new Style({
  image: new CircleStyle({
    radius: 9,
    fill: new Fill({ color: '#D97706' }), // Amber/Gold for National Capitals
    stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 2 })
  })
});

const stateCapitalStyle = new Style({
  image: new CircleStyle({
    radius: 7,
    fill: new Fill({ color: '#2563EB' }), // Blue for Regional / State Capitals
    stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 2 })
  })
});

const defaultCityStyle = new Style({
  image: new CircleStyle({
    radius: 5,
    fill: new Fill({ color: '#475569' }), // Slate gray for other populated places
    stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 1.5 })
  })
});

// 3. Dynamic Style Function with Attribute Labels
const styleFunction = (feature, resolution) => {
  const featureClass = feature.get('FEATURECLA') || feature.get('featurecla');
  const base = featureClass === 'Admin-0 capital'
    ? capitalStyle
    : (featureClass === 'Admin-1 capital' ? stateCapitalStyle : defaultCityStyle);

  // Show city labels when zoomed in (resolution < 5000 meters/pixel)
  if (resolution < 5000) {
    const cityName = feature.get('NAME') || feature.get('name') || '';
    return new Style({
      image: base.getImage(),
      text: new Text({
        text: cityName,
        font: 'bold 12px Inter, sans-serif',
        fill: new Fill({ color: '#0f172a' }),
        stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#ffffff', width: 3 }),
        offsetY: -14
      })
    });
  }

  return base;
};

// 4. Vector Dataset (Natural Earth Populated Places Sample)
// In production, load via URL: url: './data/ne_10m_populated_places.geojson'
const vectorSource = new VectorSource({
  features: new GeoJSON().readFeatures({
    type: 'FeatureCollection',
    features: [
      {
        type: 'Feature',
        properties: { NAME: 'Tokyo', ADM0NAME: 'Japan', FEATURECLA: 'Admin-0 capital', POP_MAX: 37400068 },
        geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: fromLonLat([139.6917, 35.6895]) }
      },
      {
        type: 'Feature',
        properties: { NAME: 'Delhi', ADM0NAME: 'India', FEATURECLA: 'Admin-0 capital', POP_MAX: 28514000 },
        geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: fromLonLat([77.2090, 28.6139]) }
      },
      {
        type: 'Feature',
        properties: { NAME: 'Mumbai', ADM0NAME: 'India', FEATURECLA: 'Admin-1 capital', POP_MAX: 19980000 },
        geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: fromLonLat([72.8777, 19.0760]) }
      },
      {
        type: 'Feature',
        properties: { NAME: 'London', ADM0NAME: 'United Kingdom', FEATURECLA: 'Admin-0 capital', POP_MAX: 9046485 },
        geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: fromLonLat([-0.1278, 51.5074]) }
      },
      {
        type: 'Feature',
        properties: { NAME: 'New York', ADM0NAME: 'United States', FEATURECLA: 'Populated place', POP_MAX: 8419000 },
        geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: fromLonLat([-74.0060, 40.7128]) }
      }
    ]
  })
});

const vectorLayer = new VectorLayer({
  source: vectorSource,
  style: styleFunction,
  declutter: true
});

// 5. Popup Overlay Setup
const popupContainer = document.getElementById('popup');
const popupContent = document.getElementById('popup-content');
const popupCloser = document.getElementById('popup-closer');

const overlay = new Overlay({
  element: popupContainer,
  autoPan: { animation: { duration: 250 } }
});

if (popupCloser) {
  popupCloser.onclick = () => {
    overlay.setPosition(undefined);
    popupCloser.blur();
    return false;
  };
}

// 6. Map Initialization
const map = new Map({
  target: 'map',
  layers: [baseLayer, vectorLayer],
  overlays: [overlay],
  view: new View({
    center: fromLonLat([0, 25]),
    zoom: 2
  })
});

// 7. Select Interaction
const select = new Select({
  condition: click,
  style: new Style({
    image: new CircleStyle({
      radius: 12,
      fill: new Fill({ color: '#E11D48' }), // Highlighted red on selection
      stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 3 })
    })
  })
});
map.addInteraction(select);

select.on('select', (event) => {
  const feature = event.selected[0];

  if (feature) {
    const props = feature.getProperties();
    const pop = props.POP_MAX ? Number(props.POP_MAX).toLocaleString() : 'N/A';
    popupContent.innerHTML = `
      <h4 style="margin:0 0 6px 0; font-size:14px;">${props.NAME}</h4>
      <p style="margin:0 0 4px 0; font-size:12px; color:#475569;"><strong>Country:</strong> ${props.ADM0NAME || 'N/A'}</p>
      <p style="margin:0 0 4px 0; font-size:12px; color:#475569;"><strong>Classification:</strong> ${props.FEATURECLA || 'N/A'}</p>
      <p style="margin:0; font-size:12px; color:#475569;"><strong>Population:</strong> ${pop}</p>
    `;
    overlay.setPosition(feature.getGeometry().getCoordinates());
  } else {
    overlay.setPosition(undefined);
  }
});

// 8. Hover Effect (Cursor & Stroke Highlight)
let hoveredFeature = null;
const highlightStyle = new Style({
  image: new CircleStyle({
    radius: 11,
    fill: new Fill({ color: '#00E5FF' }),
    stroke: new Stroke({ color: '#FFFFFF', width: 3 })
  })
});

map.on('pointermove', (evt) => {
  if (evt.dragging) return;

  if (hoveredFeature) {
    hoveredFeature.setStyle(null);
    hoveredFeature = null;
  }

  const hit = map.forEachFeatureAtPixel(evt.pixel, (feat, layer) => {
    if (layer === vectorLayer && !select.getFeatures().getArray().includes(feat)) {
      hoveredFeature = feat;
      feat.setStyle(highlightStyle);
      return true;
    }
  });

  map.getTargetElement().style.cursor = hit ? 'pointer' : '';
});

docs.title: Module 5 - Map Interactions & Controls
docs.text:
Welcome to Module 5! In this module, we move beyond passive map viewing and data visualization to give users full control over the map experience. You will master OpenLayers Interactions (digitizing vector geometries, editing vertices, and dragging & dropping external spatial files) and Controls (visual on-screen UI elements like scale lines, zoom sliders, coordinate readouts, and full-screen toggles).

flowchart TD
    subgraph Map Container
        Map[ol/Map Engine]

        subgraph User Input Handling
            Interactions[ol/interaction/*]
            Draw[Draw: Point / Line / Polygon / Box]
            Modify[Modify: Edit / Move / Delete Vertices]
            DragDrop[DragAndDrop: GeoJSON / KML / GPX Files]
            Snap[Snap: Topological Snapping]
            Interactions --> Draw
            Interactions --> Modify
            Interactions --> DragDrop
            Interactions --> Snap
        end

        subgraph Visual UI Elements
            Controls[ol/control/*]
            ScaleLine[ScaleLine: Metric / Bar]
            ZoomControls[Zoom / ZoomSlider / ZoomToExtent]
            FullScreen[FullScreen: HTML5 Fullscreen API]
            MousePos[MousePosition: Live Coordinate Readout]
            Overview[OverviewMap: Inset Mini-Map]
            Controls --> ScaleLine
            Controls --> ZoomControls
            Controls --> FullScreen
            Controls --> MousePos
            Controls --> Overview
        end

        Interactions --> Map
        Controls --> Map
    end

docs.title: 1. Interactions vs. Controls
docs.text:
Before writing code, understand the architectural separation of concerns in OpenLayers:

Concept Base Class Primary Purpose Examples Interactions ol/interaction/Interaction Responds to mouse, touch, pointer, and keyboard gestures to alter map navigation or mutate geometry coordinates directly. Draw, Modify, DragAndDrop, Snap, Translate, Select Controls ol/control/Control Fixed visual DOM elements positioned over the map viewport that provide status indicators or one-click commands. ScaleLine, Zoom, ZoomSlider, FullScreen, MousePosition, OverviewMap

docs.title: 2. Map Interactions: Digitizing & Editing Vector Data
docs.text: OpenLayers provides an extensive suite of digitizing interactions that allow users to draw, edit, and manipulate spatial vector features in the browser.

docs.title: 2.1 The Draw Interaction (ol/interaction/Draw)
docs.text:
The Draw interaction captures mouse or touch clicks and converts them into OpenLayers Feature geometries stored in an underlying VectorSource.

import Draw, { createBox } from 'ol/interaction/Draw.js';

// Instantiate drawing interaction for Polygons
const draw = new Draw({
  source: vectorSource,
  type: 'Polygon'
});

map.addInteraction(draw);

docs.title: Supported Drawing Geometry Types:
docs.text:
• 'Point': Places a single coordinate feature on click.
  • 'LineString': Draws connected line segments; double-click or enter to finish.
  • 'Polygon': Draws a closed boundary; double-click to close and finish.
  • 'Circle': Draws a circular geometry defined by a center coordinate and edge radius.
  • 'MultiPoint', 'MultiLineString', 'MultiPolygon': Draws multi-part geometries.

docs.title: Freehand Drawing
docs.text:
For pencil/scribble digitizing, set freehand: true: 

const freehandDraw = new Draw({
  source: vectorSource,
  type: 'LineString',
  freehand: true
});

docs.title: Drawing Rectangles / Bounding Boxes
docs.text:
To draw rectangular bounding boxes, set type: 'Circle' and use the built-in createBox() geometry function: 

import Draw, { createBox } from 'ol/interaction/Draw.js';

const boxDraw = new Draw({
  source: vectorSource,
  type: 'Circle',
  geometryFunction: createBox()
});

docs.title: Capturing Draw Events
docs.text:
Listen to drawstart and drawend lifecycle events to attach attributes or perform calculations: 

draw.on('drawstart', (event) => {
  console.log('User started drawing a geometry...');
});

draw.on('drawend', (event) => {
  const feature = event.feature;
  feature.set('createdAt', new Date().toISOString());
  console.log('Finished drawing feature:', feature.getGeometry().getType());
});

docs.title: 2.2 The Modify Interaction (ol/interaction/Modify)
docs.text:
The Modify interaction enables editing existing geometries by clicking and dragging their vertices or inserting new vertices along line segments.

import Modify from 'ol/interaction/Modify.js';

const modify = new Modify({
  source: vectorSource
});

map.addInteraction(modify);

docs.title: Key Capabilities of Modify:
docs.text:
1. Move an Existing Vertex: Click and drag any existing point/vertex.
  2. Insert a New Vertex: Hovering over a line segment or polygon boundary displays a ghost midpoint. Click and drag this midpoint to insert a new vertex.
  3. Delete a Vertex: By default, pressing Alt + clicking an existing vertex removes it. You can customize this shortcut using deleteCondition: 
    import { altKeyOnly } from 'ol/events/condition.js';

const modify = new Modify({
  source: vectorSource,
  deleteCondition: altKeyOnly // Hold Alt and click a vertex to remove it
});

docs.title: Modify Lifecycle Events:
docs.text:
modify.on('modifyend', (event) => {
  const modifiedFeatures = event.features.getArray();
  console.log(`Updated ${modifiedFeatures.length} features!`);
});

docs.title: 2.3 Topological Precision: The Snap Interaction (ol/interaction/Snap)
docs.text:
When digitizing adjacent parcels or connecting pipelines, human pointer movements are rarely pixel-perfect. The Snap interaction automatically snaps the cursor to existing vertices and edges within a configurable pixel radius:

import Snap from 'ol/interaction/Snap.js';

const snap = new Snap({
  source: vectorSource,
  pixelTolerance: 12 // Snap when cursor comes within 12px of existing vertices
});

// Always add Snap AFTER Draw and Modify interactions!
map.addInteraction(snap);

Order of Interactions: Always add Snap to the map after adding Draw or Modify. OpenLayers evaluates interactions in reverse order of addition; having Snap execute first ensures the cursor coordinate snaps before the draw or modify interaction processes the click.

docs.title: 2.4 The DragAndDrop Interaction (ol/interaction/DragAndDrop)
docs.text:
The DragAndDrop interaction enables users to drag spatial files directly from their operating system desktop and drop them onto the map canvas. OpenLayers automatically parses the file and instantiates vector features.

import DragAndDrop from 'ol/interaction/DragAndDrop.js';
import GeoJSON from 'ol/format/GeoJSON.js';
import KML from 'ol/format/KML.js';
import GPX from 'ol/format/GPX.js';

const dragAndDrop = new DragAndDrop({
  formatConstructors: [
    GeoJSON,
    KML,
    GPX
  ]
});

dragAndDrop.on('addfeatures', (event) => {
  // Features are automatically reprojected to the map view projection!
  vectorSource.addFeatures(event.features);

  // Zoom view to fit dropped features
  map.getView().fit(vectorSource.getExtent(), {
    padding: [40, 40, 40, 40],
    duration: 600
  });
});

map.addInteraction(dragAndDrop);

docs.title: Why DragAndDrop is Powerful:
docs.text:
• Zero Server Overhead: Files are parsed purely client-side in the browser using HTML5 File API and OpenLayers format parsers.
  • Automatic Reprojection: When given the view projection, coordinates are transformed automatically into the map's current coordinate system (EPSG:3857).

docs.title: 3. Map Controls: Enhancing the User Interface
docs.text:
Map controls provide visual context, navigation shortcuts, and metadata overlays.

Map Viewport
 ├── Top-Left:      Zoom Controls (+ / -), FullScreen, ZoomSlider
 ├── Top-Right:     OverviewMap (Mini-Map Inset)
 ├── Bottom-Left:   ScaleLine (Metric / Nautical / Imperial)
 └── Bottom-Right:  MousePosition (Coordinates), Attribution

docs.title: 3.1 Managing Default Controls
docs.text:
By default, OpenLayers automatically includes: - Zoom (+ and - buttons) - Rotate (bearing reset button when map is rotated) - Attribution (collapsible copyright notice)

You can customize or disable default controls using defaults() from ol/control/defaults.js:

import { defaults as defaultControls } from 'ol/control/defaults.js';
import ScaleLine from 'ol/control/ScaleLine.js';
import FullScreen from 'ol/control/FullScreen.js';

const map = new Map({
  target: 'map',
  layers: [baseLayer],
  view: new View({ /* ... */ }),
  // Extend default controls with additional controls
  controls: defaultControls({
    zoom: true,
    rotate: true,
    attribution: true
  }).extend([
    new ScaleLine(),
    new FullScreen()
  ])
});

docs.title: 3.2 The ScaleLine Control (ol/control/ScaleLine)
docs.text:
The ScaleLine control displays the real-world ground distance corresponding to screen pixels at the current zoom level and latitude.

import ScaleLine from 'ol/control/ScaleLine.js';

const scaleLine = new ScaleLine({
  units: 'metric',        // 'metric' (m/km), 'imperial' (ft/mi), 'nautical' (nm), 'degrees'
  bar: true,              // Displays a graphical segmented bar instead of a simple line
  steps: 4,               // Number of segments in the scale bar
  text: true,             // Displays distance numbers above segments
  minWidth: 140           // Minimum pixel width of the control
});

map.addControl(scaleLine);

docs.title: Customizing ScaleLine Appearance with CSS:
docs.text:
.ol-scale-line {
  background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.75);
  border-radius: 6px;
  padding: 4px 8px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
}

.ol-scale-bar {
  border-color: #38bdf8;
}

docs.title: 1. Standard Zoom Control (ol/control/Zoom)
docs.text:
import Zoom from 'ol/control/Zoom.js';

const zoomControl = new Zoom({
  zoomInLabel: '+',
  zoomOutLabel: '−',
  zoomInTipLabel: 'Zoom In',
  zoomOutTipLabel: 'Zoom Out'
});

docs.title: 2. ZoomSlider Control (ol/control/ZoomSlider)
docs.text:
The ZoomSlider displays an interactive draggable slider bar between the zoom buttons: 

import ZoomSlider from 'ol/control/ZoomSlider.js';

const zoomSlider = new ZoomSlider();
map.addControl(zoomSlider);

docs.title: 3. ZoomToExtent Control (ol/control/ZoomToExtent)
docs.text:
Provides a "Home Extent" button that resets the map view to a specified bounding box: 

import ZoomToExtent from 'ol/control/ZoomToExtent.js';
import { fromLonLat } from 'ol/proj.js';

const homeExtentButton = new ZoomToExtent({
  extent: [
    ...fromLonLat([73.7, 18.4]), // [minX, minY]
    ...fromLonLat([74.0, 18.6])  // [maxX, maxY]
  ],
  label: '⌂',
  tipLabel: 'Fit to City Bounds'
});

map.addControl(homeExtentButton);

docs.title: 3.4 The FullScreen Control (ol/control/FullScreen)
docs.text:
The FullScreen control utilizes the HTML5 Fullscreen API to expand the map container to fill the entire physical display.

import FullScreen from 'ol/control/FullScreen.js';

const fullScreenControl = new FullScreen({
  tipLabel: 'Toggle Fullscreen Mode'
});

map.addControl(fullScreenControl);

Tip: If your map has external UI control panels outside the #map <div>, specify the common parent container as the fullscreen target using source: 'app-container'.

docs.title: 1. MousePosition (ol/control/MousePosition)
docs.text:
Displays dynamic coordinates of the cursor in real time. You can format the coordinates into Longitude/Latitude degrees using createStringXY:

import MousePosition from 'ol/control/MousePosition.js';
import { createStringXY } from 'ol/coordinate.js';

const mousePosition = new MousePosition({
  coordinateFormat: createStringXY(4), // 4 decimal places (e.g. 73.8567, 18.5204)
  projection: 'EPSG:4326',             // Output in WGS 84 Lon/Lat degrees
  className: 'custom-mouse-position',
  target: document.getElementById('coordinates-display'), // Render in dedicated HTML element
  undefinedHTML: 'Coordinates: Point outside map'
});

map.addControl(mousePosition);

docs.title: 2. OverviewMap (ol/control/OverviewMap)
docs.text:
Displays an inset mini-map in the corner showing the larger geographic area and a rectangle representing the current viewport:

import OverviewMap from 'ol/control/OverviewMap.js';
import TileLayer from 'ol/layer/Tile.js';
import OSM from 'ol/source/OSM.js';

const overviewMap = new OverviewMap({
  layers: [
    new TileLayer({
      source: new OSM()
    })
  ],
  collapsed: false, // Start expanded
  collapsible: true
});

map.addControl(overviewMap);

docs.title: 4. Building a Custom OpenLayers Control
docs.text:
Any standard DOM element can be turned into an OpenLayers control by subclassing or instantiating ol/control/Control.

import { Control } from 'ol/control.js';
import { fromLonLat } from 'ol/proj.js';

class HomeControl extends Control {
  constructor(opt_options) {
    const options = opt_options || {};

    // 1. Create button element
    const button = document.createElement('button');
    button.innerHTML = '🎯';
    button.title = 'Reset to City Center';

    // 2. Wrap inside control div
    const element = document.createElement('div');
    element.className = 'ol-unselectable ol-control reset-center-control';
    element.appendChild(button);

    super({
      element: element,
      target: options.target
    });

    // 3. Handle click
    button.addEventListener('click', () => {
      this.getMap().getView().animate({
        center: fromLonLat([73.8567, 18.5204]),
        zoom: 14,
        duration: 800
      });
    });
  }
}

map.addControl(new HomeControl());

docs.title: Objective:
docs.text: Build an interactive GIS Digitizing & Map Navigation application: 1. Provide an OpenStreetMap base layer with an editable vector digitizing layer. 2. Build an on-screen toolbar to switch interaction modes: - Navigate: Pan and zoom freely. - Draw Point: Digitize point locations. - Draw LineString: Digitize routes. - Draw Polygon: Digitize land parcels. 3. Add a DragAndDrop interaction that accepts local .geojson files (test with your converted Natural Earth files like ne_10m_populated_places.geojson or ne_10m_roads.geojson), renders them on the map, and zooms to their extent. 4. Add controls: ScaleLine (metric bar), FullScreen, ZoomSlider, and live MousePosition coordinate readouts.
